title: atlas-search + fleet-search: parse_cursor panics on malformed cursors (odd-length / non-ASCII) instead of returning 400

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
# atlas-search + fleet-search: `parse_cursor` panics on malformed cursors instead of returning 400

## Evidence

`parse_cursor` decodes the client-supplied results-paging cursor by slicing
the string at byte offsets with no length or ASCII-hex gate:

- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs:1723-1735`
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs:1723-1735` (byte-identical twin)

```rust
let bytes: Result<Vec<u8>, _> = (0..cursor.len())
    .step_by(2)
    .map(|i| u8::from_str_radix(&cursor[i..i + 2], 16))
    .collect();
```

The cursor arrives from the HTTP request (caller at `server.rs:1632`,
`Some(c) => parse_cursor(c)?`) in the results-paging handler. The connection
is served on a per-connection thread (`server.rs:1980`) with no
`catch_unwind` around routing, so a panic kills the thread and drops the
connection instead of producing the function's own documented
`400 "malformed cursor"` error.

Verified this run on the laptop at main `151c8e7e1c` with a probe crate
(`~/git/fleet/probe-cursor-hex`, function copied verbatim, minimal
`ServerError` stub):

- control: valid `format_cursor(42)` roundtrip → `Ok(42)`
- control: even-length non-hex `"zzzz"` → `Err(malformed cursor)`
- control: empty string → `Err(malformed cursor)`
- odd-length hex (valid cursor minus its last character) → **PANIC**
  (slice index out of range at the final pair)
- single character `"a"` → **PANIC**
- hex pair prefix + multibyte input (`"6162a\u{e9}"`) → **PANIC**
  (slice at a non-char-boundary byte offset)

This is the same ungated-hex-parser class as #7750 (fixed in #7757 for
`local_claims::hex_bytes`): the sibling parsers there carry an
`is_ascii_hexdigit` gate per #2517; `parse_cursor` in both copies has none.
`u8::from_str_radix` also accepts a leading `+`, so even where a malformed
pair does not panic it is not validated as hex before decoding.

## Why it matters

Any client (or any corrupted/proxied request) that sends an odd-length or
non-ASCII `cursor` query value crashes its connection thread with a panic
instead of receiving the designed 400. Panics on untrusted input are a
robustness/DoS surface and produce panic noise in server logs; the cursor
is explicitly documented as opaque client-held state, so malformed values
are expected input, not an internal invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both copies (`atlas-search` and `fleet-search` `server.rs`) refuse a
      cursor whose length is odd or that contains any non-ASCII-hexdigit
      byte, returning `Err(bad_request("malformed cursor"))` — no panic on
      any input, including multibyte UTF-8.
- [ ] Valid cursors produced by `format_cursor` still roundtrip to the
      same offset in both copies.
- [ ] Regression tests cover at least: odd-length hex, single character,
      multibyte/non-boundary input, even-length non-hex, and the valid
      roundtrip — in both crates (or in the crate(s) where the handler
      lives, with the twin kept byte-identical in behavior).
- [ ] No other behavior of the results-paging handler changes (offset
      beyond end still returns its existing 400).
